thread:
Maya (CS): Heads up — ACME (acct: acme-corp) disputed January invoice INV-20260131-ACME. Invoice shows 1,210,432 tokens billed; dashboard shows 971,204. Need billing + infra help to reconcile :eyes:
Sam (Support): Thanks — can you drop the account id + invoice PDF? Any recent plan tier change?
Maya (CS): account id: acct_001ACME; invoice: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/INV-20260131-ACME; dashboard snapshot: https://dash.redwood.ai/orgs/acme/usage?range=Jan
Eli (BillingEng): Pinging in — I'll pull the meter-run artifacts. Did we run any reprocessing around 2026-01-31T23:50Z..2026-02-01T02:10Z?
billing-bot: meter-run completed for window 2026-01-01..2026-01-31 at 2026-02-01T02:03:12Z; job_id: mr_20260201_002; files_processed: 122; status: success
Anna (Infra): FYI we had a batch retry spike on 2026-02-01T01:59Z due to transient S3 throttling — lambda retries caused duplicate SNS deliveries for ~5m
Eli (BillingEng): That would explain duplicates. Can someone run this to find dup ingestion_event_ids for acct_001ACME?
```
SELECT ingestion_event_id, count(*) as cnt
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_001ACME'
  AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-01-31 23:55:00+00' AND '2026-02-01 02:10:00+00'
GROUP BY ingestion_event_id
HAVING count(*) > 1
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Sam (Support): Running — will paste results in a sec
Sam (Support): returned 48 rows; top dup count = 3; roughly 1,324 events duplicated across that window
Eli (BillingEng): Ok. Can you sample raw events for ingestion_event_id to see request_id / retry headers? We need to know if duplicates were client retries or server-side redeliveries
Sam (Support): sample:
```
{ "ingestion_event_id": "evt_abc123", "request_id": "req_NX-991", "retry_attempt": 1, "tokens": 64 }
{ "ingestion_event_id": "evt_abc123", "request_id": "req_NX-991", "retry_attempt": 2, "tokens": 64 }
```
Maya (CS): Customer says they didn't trigger retries — they're on our hosted API with no SDK auto-retry
Anna (Infra): Root cause: our S3->ingest lambda redelivered same SNS message because of at-least-once semantics and a bug where the dedupe header (x-rw-ingest-id) was dropped under high concurrency. Patch to restore header handling merged (PR #3124) and deployed 2026-02-02T05:40Z
Eli (BillingEng): For remediation we should: 1) mark mr_20260201_002 as reprocess_pending; 2) run dedupe across ingestion_event_id keeping latest; 3) recompute token aggregates and regenerate line items; 4) issue credit if delta material. I'll queue a reprocess job.
Sam (Support): Quick est: 1,324 dup events * avg 64 tokens ~= 84.7k tokens => ~$34. Small but confirms dupes exist
billing-bot: reprocess job queued: reprocess_job_id: rp_20260203_001 for acct_001ACME; started 2026-02-03T09:10:01Z
Sam (Support): Reprocess finished. Regenerated invoice tokens: 1,204,320 -> 971,548 (delta 232,772). That's larger than the initial dup set estimate
Eli (BillingEng): Hmm. Looking deeper: we also had an aggregation normalization bug that double-counted events arriving near midnight UTC, causing overlap between mr_20260201_002 and mr_20260202_002 windows. Checking aggregator logs now
Anna (Infra): Confirmed. Timestamp normalization applied twice for events near 2026-01-31 23:58..00:02 leading to overlapping bucket membership. Fix merged in PR #3140 (2026-02-02T11:12Z)
Maya (CS): Customer needs a clear explanation and the credit + adjusted invoice. What's the final delta and proposed credit?
Eli (BillingEng): Final after dedupe+overlap fix: corrected tokens = 977,660 (from 1,210,432). Net delta = 232,772 tokens. At our rate that's ~$93.11. I'll open a CIT with full diffs, PR links, and reprocess audit. Recommend pro-rated credit and a short RC explanation: "duplicate ingestion deliveries plus aggregation window overlap caused double-counting at month boundary."
Sam (Support): I'll draft the customer-facing message and coordinate with Finance. Maya — can you review?
Maya (CS): Will review and send today. Thanks everyone :pray:
Eli (BillingEng): Follow-ups: (1) run a global scan to detect other accounts with similar dup clusters; (2) add a meter-run validation to alert when dashboard vs invoice differs >10%; (3) add unit tests for timestamp normalization
Anna (Infra): Added infra-monitoring alert for lambda retry spikes during meter windows. Also added a small rate limiter to prevent redelivery storms
Maya (CS): CC'ing finance: @finance
Finance (Finance): Seen — include the CIT ID and final token diff so we can attach credit to INV-20260131-ACME
Eli (BillingEng): CIT-20260203-17 created. Attached reprocess logs and final diff. Finance to process credit and close. Closing thread after credit posts.
